items.text: Completely agree.  I'm not a fan, at least assuming you are talking about the current production blood slayer.  I haven't tried the old Chubby.  Besides what was said above, I really don't care for the kicks and the wheelbase is longer than I'd like.  The Elixir, or many others, would be my suggestion.
I definitely find that sand and pretty much anything loose on the road makes slides much less predictable and more prone to icing out.

Sounds like hard carving.  Kinda works, but hard to rely on, as it depends on having the space and a shallow enough grade.  Foot braking, which it sounds like you have already discovered, is very effective, as is sliding.
I wouldn't wash your wheels.  Probably not a big deal, but the urethane does react a bit with water.  I'd just wipe the cores down if they are gross, if you really want to.
Whichever of Alternative's boards from last year appeals most, or Zenit, especially in the b-grade section.

Yeah, it be like that.  Don't grab rail between your legs, grab over and behind your rear leg (if you feel you even need to grab, I often do only until I reach the apex of the precarve and then let go), and transfer a lot more of your weight forward to the front foot.  Many find it helpful to lay the rear foot down on its side, which doesn't feel super natural but is made much easier by moving your weight further forward than you may expect.  This will help deweight the rear, allowing it to start sliding.
Yeah, it feels more natural to many, but doesn't promote the right weight distribution.  Glad the scrapes weren't too bad, slide gloves ftw!
What grip tape do you use? Leather and suede last much better than fabric.   A vegan friend uses shoe glue to reinforce his.

Started on some v3 swingers a few weeks ago and they seem much grippier than the v2 I killed last year.  I assume it is because of the larger core, but could be temperature.  Wearing much more slowly too, and not as much sugery fun.
duct tape under the grip?

What are you doing that scratches it, riding off curbs, or roads with lots of debris?  For the former, leveling out with the tail helps a lot.  Latter, try and avoid stuff, and maybe look at bigger wheels.
its a double drop, and quite drifty.  Easy to slide, but sometimes a little too easy.  Pretty good choice for what you are wanting, definitely easy to push.

I find curbs are my largest source of scratches. If you just ride up/down, the bottom often rubs. You can counter this going off by doing kinda a manual, lifting the nose slightly with the tail so it doesn't scrape as it tilts off. Going up, learn to Ollie or grab or something maybe? I need to work on that still.
Very cool, how did you make it?  Carbon top and bottom with balsa core?  Any concave?
Loved it, one of the best skate films I have seen in recent memory.

For 5 minute commutes, you can ride pretty much anything, but a top mount with w concave would be my last choice for pushing (Tesseract).  Sportster is nice and low, easy for long distances, and easy to use with large wheels.  The Maestro is low enough that I have done many marathons without issue, and I can get 72mm wheels on it easily.  You can slide on any of those, but the Tesseract will be the best, being top mount with w concave.  You will probably have issues putting large wheels on it without a lot of riser, unless you are good with restrictive bushing setups and/or wheelbite.  The Maestro (at least my tg) slides quite smoothly, where the Sportster feels a bit loose, very drifty, and would be my last choice at speed, but fine <30mph.
Mine is the thermoglass variant, so a bit different feel and shape than the e-core.

You want wheels which won't chunk or have the core explode on impact from landing tricks which leave the ground, stoneground finish to let it slide more easily/smoothly, relatively small and light (<66mm generally) for weight and balance.  Depending what you are doing though, different characteristics may or may not matter.  If you are only board walking, you can probably use whatever.  Really depends what dancing means to you, and what gives you the feel you want.

items.title: Mountains or Ocean?
items.text: Mountains or Ocean?

My buddy has an ecore Maestro, and it doesn't feel super flexy the couple times I stood on it, but I haven't tried any slides yet.  I vaguely remember the concave being a bit sharper, and not in a way I particularly cared for.  I haven't really felt that super aggressive concave is necessary to slide, but it can give you good reference points to know where you are on your board, which is important.  Here is some 'thane from my maestro pro for reference: [https://i.imgur.com/V9BJLaq.jpg](https://i.imgur.com/V9BJLaq.jpg)

Same buddy also has the bamboo-x sportster, which I had forgotten is 2" shorter than the ecore.  Slides easily, but kinda just lets loose.  I recently received a dualomo e-board, which uses an e-core thermoglass sportster for the deck, and agree that the longer wheelbase makes it kinda dead.  The few slides I have tried on it weren't great, as you say it isn't as easy to carve into slides, but also its an 18lb brick with full skin on the wheels and I haven't finished dialing it.  I like my trucks quite loose, and have generally been able to compensate enough that way and with weight distribution.  Neither the Maestro or Sportster are flexy in the way that something like a Loaded Icarus or Dervish is, and I have never felt like it was causing an issue for low speed freeride.

I wouldn't get any of those if you intend to dance on it.  I'd go with a full topmount double kick, >100cm long. Shorter for responsive steering and freestyle tricks, longer for more boardwalking.
Think my Avitar took about 2 months to manufacture and ship past summer. It's really nice.

Length is fine, but it is a drop through, which is good for cruising but not for dancing or freestyle. You get much less effective footspace, it's far easier to step on the wheels, especially when trying to use the tails, and the neck can break much more easily.
With a minimum wheelbase of 84cm, it's gonna steer like a boat. Hard to navigate through tight spaces.

Pumping, freestyle tricks, or what?  AN6-24a aircraft bolts work well for standard longboard bushings, or grade 8 3/8-24 in the 2.6" range.
